investigations.title: Percutaneous coronary angiography
investigations.summary: Invasive coronary catheter angiography: assess anatomy, stenoses and flow, then document adjunctive tests, PCI when performed, complications and handover.
source_titles: SCAI expert consensus update on best practices in the cardiac catheterization laboratory (2021)
ACC/AHA/SCAI structured reporting for the cardiac catheterization laboratory (2014)
2025 Acute Coronary Syndromes guideline: key points

protocol: Confirm indication, consent and the institutional pre-procedure assessment.
Record access, equipment, drugs, contrast exposure and radiation from the actual procedural record.
Assess adequate projections of each coronary territory; document missing coverage.

checklist.label: Access and acquisition
checklist.detail: Establish what was performed and the available angiographic runs.

checklist.label: Origins, course and dominance
checklist.detail: Describe the coronary tree before individual lesions.

checklist.label: Lesion by lesion
checklist.detail: Localize disease and record the method and confidence of assessment.

checklist.label: Additional assessments
checklist.detail: Report adjunctive tests only when acquired.

checklist.label: PCI result, when applicable
checklist.detail: Document the target and final result separately from the diagnostic findings.

checklist.label: Complications and immediate handover
checklist.detail: Record the outcome and information needed by the receiving team.

measurements.name: Contrast volume and radiation
measurements.method: Record mL, dose-area product and reference air kerma with units, plus fluoroscopy time.
measurements.pitfall: Time alone is not a complete radiation dose record.

measurements.name: Coronary stenosis
measurements.method: Report segment, percent diameter narrowing and visual or quantitative method.
measurements.pitfall: Avoid false precision in a poorly profiled vessel.

measurements.name: Adjunctive measurements
measurements.method: Record vessel, value, units or ratio, and acquisition conditions for tests performed.
measurements.pitfall: Do not infer FFR / iFR from angiographic appearance.

steps.tip: Foreshortening and overlap can conceal disease; explicitly identify segments that cannot be assessed.

steps.heading: LESIONS AND FLOW
steps.label: Lesion by lesion
steps.detail: Localize disease and record the method and confidence of assessment.
steps.body:
For each lesion: vessel / segment [ ]; narrowing [ ]%; visual / quantitative method [ ]; length [ ] mm if measured; calcification / thrombus / bifurcation / occlusion [ ].

Collateral supply: [ ].
steps.look: Review the tightest segment in more than one adequate projection and compare with the reference vessel.
steps.tip: A luminal stenosis estimate alone does not establish physiological significance. CAD-RADS is a coronary CT system.

steps.heading: PHYSIOLOGY AND INTRAVASCULAR IMAGING
steps.label: Additional assessments
steps.detail: Report adjunctive tests only when acquired.
steps.body:

steps.look: Match every pressure or intravascular measurement to its vessel and acquisition record.
steps.tip: Keep anatomical severity and physiological assessment distinct.

steps.look: Compare the pre-intervention and final runs using the same target vessel.
steps.tip: Do not turn a diagnostic angiography worksheet into an implied instruction to intervene.

investigations.title: Echocardiography — adult transthoracic study
investigations.summary: Adult resting TTE: organize acoustic windows, chamber function, valve Doppler, filling assessment and pericardial findings into a structured report.
source_titles: ASE standardization of adult echocardiography reporting (2025)
ASE comprehensive transthoracic echocardiography in adults (2019)

protocol: Record indication, examination scope, physiological context and image quality.
Acquire standard 2D and Doppler views appropriate to a comprehensive adult TTE.
Identify unassessed structures; use a dedicated protocol for TEE, stress or congenital studies.

checklist.label: Scope and acoustic windows
checklist.detail: Identify the study type and whether the clinical question can be answered.

checklist.label: LV size and systolic function
checklist.detail: Assess chamber size, global function and regional contraction.

checklist.label: RV and atrial assessment
checklist.detail: Describe chamber size and right ventricular function.

checklist.label: Valve morphology and haemodynamics
checklist.detail: Integrate morphology, Doppler and chamber response.

checklist.label: Filling, pericardium and other findings
checklist.detail: Integrate filling assessment and complete the structural survey.

checklist.label: Comparison and communication
checklist.detail: Answer the clinical question and state meaningful interval change.

measurements.name: LV volumes and ejection fraction
measurements.method: Record end-diastolic / end-systolic volumes, indexing and EF method.

measurements.name: RV function and pressure estimates
measurements.method: Record measures used, TR velocity / IVC assumptions where applicable.
measurements.pitfall: Do not report an unsupported pressure estimate.

measurements.name: Valve Doppler and aortic dimensions
measurements.method: Record velocity, gradients and integrated severity data; name aortic measurement level.
measurements.pitfall: Doppler misalignment and inconsistent measurement conventions alter results.

measurements.name: Diastolic parameters
measurements.method: Record the acquired inflow, tissue Doppler and supporting measurements.
measurements.pitfall: Use an applicable guideline and report indeterminate assessment when appropriate.

pitfalls: Apical foreshortening and poor border definition alter volume estimates.
Interpret Doppler with rhythm, loading conditions and acquisition quality.
A resting TTE does not exclude coronary artery disease.
escalation: Communicate suspected tamponade physiology, acute severe valve dysfunction or other critical haemodynamic findings promptly.
